title: Did the Quran Predict Internal Waves in the Ocean?
description:
When the Titan submersible imploded near the Titanic wreck in June 2023, a tragedy that shocked the world was quickly hijacked by religious apologists. WhatsApp forwards and YouTube shorts claimed the Quran had already described the darkness of the deep sea 1,400 years ago — proof, they said, of “Islamic science.”

But is it true? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we debunk these pseudoscientific claims by examining:

The Titan disaster and how science explained what happened.

The Quranic verse (Surah An-Nur 24:40) used to “prove” oceanography.

The viral debate between EA Jabbar and MM Akbar, which dismantled such miracle claims years earlier.

The deceptive methods of Islamic apologetics and the infamous Zindani Project, which misled even Western scientists.

Why myths about internal ocean waves and “scientific miracles” in scripture collapse under scrutiny.

How tragedies are exploited to push pseudoscience and blind faith.

👉 If you’ve searched for Titan sub disaster explained, Titan submarine implosion, Quran scientific miracles debunked, Surah An-Nur 24:40 explained, EA Jabbar debate MM Akbar, Islamic science exposed — this video reveals the truth.

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

The Quran is scientifically and factually wrong. The heart is NOT the source of emotions, desire or wisdom. This is clearly the CARDIOCENTRIC HYPOTHESIS. It is true that cognitive or emotional elements can affect the intensity or duration of pain through mechanisms which I will explain later. But this has got NOTHING to do with the heart. This will be clear when I explain the different pathways of somatic and visceral pain.

Secondly, the neurons in the heart are just clustered into a few ganglia. A ganglion is a group of neuronal cell bodies. The exact functions of these ganglia are still UNKNOWN. The only thing we know is that these ganglia may regulate the rate and rhythm of the heartbeat.

The MAIN CONTROL of the HEART resides with the MEDULLA OBLANGATA.  There is an area called the 'cardioacceleratory centre', or 'pressor centre', in the upper part of the medulla oblongata, and an area called the 'cardioinhibitory centre', or 'depressor centre', in the lower part.  Together they are called the 'CARDIOREGULATORY CENTRE', since they interact to 'CONTROL the HEART RATE'.

The nervous supply to the heart is autonomic, consisting of both sympathetic and parasympathetic parts. The sympathetic fibres arise from the pressor centre, while the parasympathetic fibres arise in the depressor centre.

The sympathetic nervous system acts on the sinoatrial node, speeding up the depolarisation rate, and therefore 'increasing the heart rate'.  The 'parasympathetic system' works in reverse order 'to slow the heart rate down'.  The heart itself has a natural pacemaker, the sinoatrial node, which does not need a nerve supply to function.  If you sever all the nerves to the heart, then it will continue to beat.   In fact, it will beat faster than normal, since there is normally a parasympathetic supply slowing the heart down.

The sympathetic fibres, arising from the superior, middle, and inferior cervical ganglia (but originating in the medulla oblongata), and the parasympathetic fibres, which originate in the medulla oblongata and pass down by way of the VAGUS NERVE, join in the cardiac plexus (which has superficial and deep parts).  From here they enter the heart.

Now there is a grave misconception that the heart is the centre of emotions. This is a pre-scientific notion. We have the LIMBIC SYSTEM of the brain which is responsible for establishing emotion, memory storage and retrieval and our consciousness. In fact, the whole cortex is responsible for our consciousness or mind.

Another region called INSULAR CORTEX plays a role in certain higher-level functions that operate only in humans and other great apes. It's involved in cognitive-emotional processes, empathy, compassion, meta-cognitive emotions(awareness of one's thought processes and an understanding of the patterns behind them), homeostasis, hunger, pain, fatigue, taste, motor control, self-awareness, interpersonal experience interoception(collection of senses understanding the internal state of the body), timing one's heartbeat, blood pressure regulation, negative emotions, non-interoceptive perceptions like passive listening to music, laughter, crying, empathy, language etc. NONE of these functions have anything to do with the heart.


 
Now let's talk about fear and anxiety.
The 'amygdala' plays an important role in mediating responses to fear and anxiety. Similarly the 'insular cortex' is also involved in producing anxiety. Patients with anxiety disorders have been found to show heightened amygdala response to anxiety cues. The amygdala and limbic system structures are connected to the prefrontal cortex regions. The prefrontal cortex is the "thinking brain" that perceives danger, stress or threats.

For instance, when our "thinking brain" senses danger it communicates with the "emotional brain"(limbic system, insular cortex) to send signals which in turn activate the sympathetic nervous system which mediates all the symptoms of anxiety. Chemicals called catecholamines like adrenaline and noradrenaline are produced. These go and bind to the beta receptors in the heart cells and increase the force of contraction. Also, sympathetic activation increases heart rate. The intrinsic nervous system dubbed the "little brain of heart" work along with the autonomous nervous supply to the heart in coordinating the blood flow to meet the increased demand for blood to our brain and limbs so that we will have an increased sense of awareness and we are primed for any physical exertion. This is when you experience palpitation. And all these are the physical manifestation of anxiety. Now the average duration of a heartbeat is just 0.8s. It's no wonder that the heart constantly has to send feedback to the brain about how it is holding up under stress. Even under normal circumstances all organs directly(sense organs) or indirectly(kidney during water and electrolyte homeostasis) send signals to the brain. Even proprioceptors in our joints are continuously firing signals to let the brain know the position of our joints and to help maintain our posture during walking, running, climbing etc. So the argument that since the heart is sending more signals to the brain than vice-versa(couldn't find any evidence for this claim) the heart is in total control of the brain is fallacious. About 90 per cent of the fibres in the primary visceral nerve, the vagus, carry information from the gut to the brain and not the other way around( Dr Michael Gershon). The same can be said about any sensory organ or receptor. The receptors for touch, pressure, vibration, temperature etc in our skin are also sending more signals to the brain than it receives back. The same is true for eyes and ears.

Now in a recent study by Hseuh et,
they tried to understand if an increased heart rate can induce anxiety. They artificially increased the heart rate of mice by 36% of the baseline using an optogenetic (light) pacemaker. They found that an increase in heart rate alone DIDN'T cause noticeable anxious behaviour in the mice but when the mice sensed HINTS OF DANGER such as a large, uncovered area, a higher heart rate made them stick closer to the walls ( because mice naturally prefer darker enclosed spaces as they feel more safe). And, given the opportunity to press a lever for water, a higher heart rate made them less likely to do so if the lever occasionally delivered a minor shock. When it comes to anxiety, the researchers found, CONTEXT MATTERED. Next, when they inhibited the 'insular cortex', the anxious behaviour generated by a racing heart NEARLY  VANISHED. This once again proves that the brain is the centre of interoception-the ability to perceive the body’s internal states, including heart rate, hunger, temperature and pain, stress, fear, anxiety etc. If the heart was the source of emotion and anxiety the mice should've showed anxious behaviour even when the insular cortex was inactivated. But we see that the anxious behaviour VANISHED when the insular cortex was inactivated. Similarly merely increasing the heart rate didn't produce anxiety because the CONTEXT mattered. It is the "thinking brain", the PRE-FRONTAL CORTEX-the most evolved brain region-that subserves our HIGHEST ORDER COGNITIVE abilities. It is also the brain region most sensitive to the harmful effects of stress exposure. The prefrontal cortex (PFC) intelligently regulates our thoughts, actions and emotions through extensive connections with other brain regions. It creates a “mental sketch pad” through neuronal networks also referred to as working memory. PFC also connect with the insular cortex.

Nowhere in the study do the researchers say that anxiety is produced in the heart or processed in the heart. Nor did they say emotions come from the heart. The only thing this study says is that in an appropriate context ( a situation perceived by the brain as dangerous, stressful or threatening) an increase in the heart rate can be processed by the specialized areas in the brain and produce feelings of anxiety and activate its physical symptoms. Again it's the brain that makes the judgement regarding whether a context is dangerous or not, it is the brain that understands that there is an increase in heart rate and it is the brain itself that produces anxiety.

It is clear beyond any reasonable doubt that the functions of the brain are unique and can't take place in the heart let alone anywhere else in the body. Because for that to happen we need specialized differentiated neuronal systems and circuitries like the cerebral cortex. The number of neurons in the heart is minuscule when compared with the 86 billion neurons in the human brain and around 100 billion neurons in the whole central nervous system ( brain and spine). Even the ENS has 200-600 billion neurons but still can't think or help us write poems (explained later).

"Archaeologists found the 8,000-year-old pearl in 2017 while conducting excavations at Marawah Island, which is located off the west coast of the United Arab Emirates. The ancient village includes some of the oldest stone houses discovered on the Arabian Gulf; large amounts of turtle, dolphin, dugong and fish bones found at the site indicate its inhabitants were VERY FAMILIAR WITH THE SEA SURROUNDING THEM. There is also EVIDENCE they engaged in PEARLING, thus beginning a tradition that was to define the region for centuries to come. Their KNOWLEDGE OF THE SEA also allowed them to engage in MARITIME TRADE, and it is possible that pearls harvested from the sea were an important part of this".(Source: Department of Culture and Tourism Dubai, Govt of UAE)

Archaeologists not only found that the inhabitants of the Marawah islands were involved in pearl hunting but found that these people captured large amounts of turtles, dolphin, dugong(sea cow) and other sea creatures as these were found in their stone houses. Also, these people engaged in maritime trade probably to trade their pearls and other goods which needs high level of sea navigation skills, knowledge about the nature of seas like high tide and low tide, knowledge of wind and the skills to use wind favourably, know the distance between the lands across the sea in terms of the number of days required for the voyage and probably some idea about how deep the sea is at different distances from the coast. Also, from the 6th century pearling town in Siniyah Island, diving weights that help to drop to the sea bed quickly was also found. It is because of these reasons did the archaeologists confirm that the inhabitants of these pearling towns were VERY FAMILIAR WITH THE SEA SURROUNDING THEM. All this shows the knowledge that the sea progressively becomes dimmer or darker as one descends through the depths of the sea should be well-known to these inhabitants who were pearl divers, sailors and navigators, and fishers who also captured large sea mammals. It's hard to believe that no one knew this information before Quran came in the 7th century when these people existed thousands of years before the Quran. Also, this particular verse in Quran is using an analogy of darkness in the ocean to explain the state of non-believers. It says non-believers are living in darkness like the one in the ocean. Analogy is always a means of explaining hard to understand idea by drawing comparison with another idea that people are well aware of. If people are ignorant of the idea that is used as an analogy, there is absolutely no point in making that analogy. It's futile. "ആഴക്കടൽ" എന്ന വാക്കിന്റെ അർത്ഥം "deep-sea" അതായത് കടലിന്റെ ആഴത്തിലുള്ള ഭാഗം. ഇന്ന് ഗവേഷകർ ആഴക്കടൽ എന്നുകൊണ്ട് ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നത് appx.200m/656ft depth മുതലാണ്. ചുരുക്കി പറഞ്ഞാൽ ആഴക്കടൽ എന്ന വാക്ക് കൊണ്ട് ഉദ്ദേശിക്കുന്നത് കടലിന്റെ ആഴത്തിലെ ഒരു point ആണ്. പക്ഷെ ഖുർആനിൽ ഈ ആയത്തിൽ "deep-sea" അതായത് "ആഴക്കടൽ" എന്ന അർത്ഥം വരുന്ന അറബി പദം അല്ല ഉപയോഗിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത്. മറിച്ച് ഇവിടെ "കടൽ" എന്ന noun ഉപയോഗിച്ചിട്ട് അതിനെ "ആഴമുള്ള" എന്ന "adjective" അല്ലെങ്കിൽ "വിശേഷണം" ആണ് ഉപയോഗിച്ചിട്ടുള്ളത്. അതായത് ആയത്തിൽ "ആഴക്കടൽ"/"deep-sea" എന്നല്ല പറഞ്ഞിട്ടുള്ളത് മറിച്ച് "ആഴമുള്ള കടൽ"/"sea that is deep" എന്നാണ് പറഞ്ഞിട്ടുള്ളത്. ഈ രണ്ട് പ്രയോഗങ്ങൾ തമ്മിൽ കാര്യമായ "semantic differences" അതായത് ഭാഷയിലെ അർത്ഥവ്യത്യാസമുണ്ട്. ഉദാഹരണമായി "ആഴമുള്ള പുഴയിൽ മുതലയുണ്ട് "/ "പുഴയുടെ ആഴത്തിൽ മുതലയുണ്ട് " എന്ന sentences നോക്കുക. ആദ്യത്തെ വാക്യത്തിൽ പുഴ ആഴമുള്ളതാണെങ്കിലും മുതല എവിടെയെന്നു പറയുന്നില്ല. ഒരുപക്ഷെ പുഴയുടെ ഉപരിതലത്തിൽ float ചെയ്യുകയാകാം, അല്ലെങ്കിൽ പുറത്തുനിന്നു കാണാൻ പറ്റാത്ത രീതിയിൽ വെള്ളത്തിനടിയിൽ ആകാം. ആകെ കൂടി അറിയുന്ന കാര്യം പുഴ ആഴമുള്ളതാണ് അതിൽ മുതലയും ഉണ്ട്. രണ്ടാമത്തെ വാക്യത്തിൽ പുഴയുടെ ആഴമൊന്നും അറിയില്ല 1m, 5m or 10m ഏതുമാവാം. പക്ഷെ ഉറപ്പായി അറിയുന്ന കാര്യം മുതല പുഴയുടെ ആഴത്തിലാണ് എന്നുള്ളതാണ്.  പുഴയുടെ ആഴം അര മീറ്റർ ആണെങ്കിലും മുതല ആഴത്തിൽ തന്നെ. ആയത്തിൽ ആഴക്കടൽ എന്നല്ല മറിച്ച് ആഴമുള്ള കടൽ എന്നാണ് പറഞ്ഞിട്ടുള്ളത്. അതായത് ആയത്തിൽ സൂചിപ്പിക്കുന്നത് കടലിന്റെ ആഴത്തിലുള്ള ഭാഗമല്ല പക്ഷെ കടൽ ആഴമുള്ളതാണ് എന്നൊരു വിശേഷണം മാത്രമാണ്. അക്ബർ ഇത് വളച്ചൊടിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുകയാണ് കാരണം വിശ്വാസികൾക്ക് arabic grammar പോയി എന്തിന് അറബിയിൽ ഒരു അഞ്ച് വാക്യങ്ങൾ പോലും construct ചെയ്യാൻ അറിയില്ല.

2. പിന്നെ "യഗ്ശാഹു" എന്ന verb apply ആവുന്നത് "മൗജുൻ" എന്ന വാക്കിലാണ്. അക്ബർ പറയുന്ന പോലെ "ള്ളുലുമാത്തു" എന്ന വാക്കിൽ മുകളിൽ പറഞ്ഞ verb apply ആകണമെങ്കിൽ "യഗ്ശാഹ" എന്ന verb form use ചെയ്തിട്ടുണ്ടാവണം. ഇതാണ് അക്ബറിന്റെ രണ്ടാമത്തെ തന്ത്രം. "മൗജുൻ" എന്ന് വെച്ചാൽ തിരമാല, "ള്ളുലുമാത്തു" എന്ന് വെച്ചാൽ ഇരുട്ട്. "യഗ്ശാഹു" എന്ന് വെച്ചാൽ മൂടുക. അങ്ങനെ നോക്കുമ്പോ ആയത്തിൽ പറയുന്നത് തിരമാലകലാണ് "കടലിനെ" ഒന്നിന് മീതെ ഒന്നായി മൂടുന്നത്. ഇവിടെ ശ്രദ്ധിക്കേണ്ടത് "തിരമാലകൾ കടലിനെ മൂടുന്നു" എന്നാണ് ആയത്തിൽ പറയുന്നത്. അങ്ങനെയെങ്കിൽ കടലിനെ മൂടാൻ പറ്റുന്ന തിരമാലകൾ ഉപരിതലത്തിലുള്ള തിരമാലകൾ മാത്രമാണ്. ഇവിടെ ഖുർആൻ വ്യക്തമായി പറയുന്നത് കടലിനെ മൂടുന്ന കടലിന്റെ ഉപരിതലത്തിലുള്ള തിരമാലകളെ തന്നെയാണ്. പക്ഷെ "ആഴമുള്ള കടൽ" എന്നതിനെ സൗകര്യപ്പൂർവം "ആഴക്കടൽ" ആക്കി മാറ്റി "ഉപരിതലത്തിലെ തിരമാലകളെ" അങ്ങ് "ആഴകടലിലെ തിരമാലകളാക്കി"!!!!
